answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using proof-of-coverage attestation. To reject hollow virtual nodes, each agent binds its execution thread to a transceiver on an exterior ledge. Peers exchange time-stamped challenges to confirm unique physical locations via time-of-flight. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring dedicated transceivers and distinct physical sites per identity. However, RF multipath reflections can distort timing, falsely rejecting honest agents.
